questions.question: How would you solve Two Sum in Go?
questions.title: Two Sum with a map
questions.direct_answer: Scan the slice once while storing each value's index in a map. For the current value x, look for target-x before storing x; this gives O(n) time and O(n) space.

interviewer_intent.testing: Hash-map lookup, one-pass reasoning, and Go slice syntax.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Storing the current value before checking, which can reuse the same element.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: State why the complement is checked first and explain the duplicate-value case.

sections.title: What the interviewer wants
sections.content: Define Two Sum with a map simply, show a small example, and mention the main trade-off or edge case.

sections.title: Complement lookup
sections.content: For every number, the only partner that can reach the target is target minus number. A map turns that lookup into constant average time.

sections.title: Go solution
Complexity
items: Checking before inserting prevents using an element twice.

sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content: I keep previously seen values and their indexes in a map. For each number I ask whether its complement is already present; if yes, I return the two indexes, otherwise I record the number and continue.
